zh.principle: **算法**：KISS 伪随机数生成器（KISS Pseudorandom Number Generator）。KISS 把四个 32 位子生成器组合成一个 32 位输出，状态共 128 位。MWC 用两个 16 位半字更新：\(z'=36969\,(z\bmod 2^{16})+\lfloor z/2^{16}\rfloor\)，\(w'=18000\,(w\bmod 2^{16})+\lfloor w/2^{16}\rfloor\)，再把 \(z'\) 左移 16 位与 \(w'\) 相加。SHR3 做三次移位异或：先左移 17，再右移 13，再左移 5；CONG 是 \(x'=69069x+1234567\bmod 2^{32}\)。最后输出 \((MWC\oplus x')+SHR3\bmod 2^{32}\)。四个子生成器的周期互相制约，不能把单个 LCG 的 \(2^{32}\) 当成整体周期。
zh.why: KISS 是“Keep It Simple, Stupid”的缩写，目标是给模拟和统计测试提供极快、极短的 PRNG，不是分组密码。它没有密钥、没有认证、没有抗侧信道目标；把 KISS 当流密码或 CSPRNG 使用，会把“统计上像随机”误当成“不可预测”。该条目同时修正旧目录把 KISS 标成“轻量级分组密码”的错误：KISS 的状态更新是 PRNG，输出不是 \(E_K(x)\)。
zh.used: 实现时要固定四个 32 位状态的初值，并保证不全为零；每次调用按同一顺序更新 MWC、SHR3、CONG，再组合输出。验证实现时，先对已知种子复现前几个 32 位输出，再检查 \(x'\) 的模 \(2^{32}\) 回绕、MWC 的两个半字是否按 16 位切开，以及 SHR3 的移位方向。它适合蒙特卡洛、游戏草稿和测试数据；不适合密钥、nonce、会话令牌或任何需要抗预测的场景。
zh.broken: Rose 的分析给出两个关键边界：32 位 KISS 的最大周期约为 \(2^{119.5}\)，不是早期宣称的 \(2^{123}\)；从约 70 个输出字可以恢复状态，复杂度约 \(2^{29.1}\)。这说明“周期长”不等于“密码安全”。另外，64 位/256 位变体（常称 KISS64/KISS11）状态更大、周期约 \(2^{247}\)，但仍是统计 PRNG；不能把不同变体的参数混到 32 位 KISS 的公式里。
zh.history:
Marsaglia 与 Zaman 在 1993 年提出 KISS 类组合思路，1998 年的 C 版本把 LCG、SHR3 和两个 MWC 拼成四字状态；Rose 在 2018 年给出系统分析，指出周期上界与状态恢复攻击。2009 年出现的 64 位 KISS 把状态扩到 256 位，周期约 \(2^{247}\)。本站 R128 同时把条目标题从“轻量级分组密码”改为“伪随机数生成器”，因为原分类与算法事实不符。

en.principle: **Algorithm**: KISS Pseudorandom Number Generator (KISS 伪随机数生成器). KISS combines four 32-bit sub-generators into one 32-bit output over a 128-bit state. MWC updates two 16-bit halves: \(z'=36969\,(z\bmod 2^{16})+\lfloor z/2^{16}\rfloor\), \(w'=18000\,(w\bmod 2^{16})+\lfloor w/2^{16}\rfloor\), then shifts \(z'\) left by 16 and adds \(w'\). SHR3 applies three shift-xor steps: left 17, right 13, left 5. CONG is \(x'=69069x+1234567\bmod 2^{32}\). The output is \((MWC\oplus x')+SHR3\bmod 2^{32}\). The sub-generator periods constrain one another; a single LCG period \(2^{32}\) is not the whole period.
en.why: KISS means “Keep It Simple, Stupid” and targets a very fast, very short PRNG for simulation and statistical tests, not a block cipher. It has no key, authentication or side-channel goal; using KISS as a stream cipher or CSPRNG mistakes “statistically random” for “unpredictable”. This card also corrects the old catalog label “lightweight block cipher”: KISS updates a PRNG state, and its output is not \(E_K(x)\).
en.used:
An implementation fixes four 32-bit initial states, never all zero, then updates MWC, SHR3 and CONG in the same order and combines the outputs. To verify, reproduce the first few 32-bit outputs from a known seed, then check the \(x'\) wrap at \(2^{32}\), the 16-bit split in MWC and the SHR3 shift directions. It suits Monte Carlo, game drafts and test data; it does not suit keys, nonces, session tokens or anything requiring unpredictability.

en.broken: Rose gives two key boundaries: the 32-bit KISS maximum period is about \(2^{119.5}\), not the earlier \(2^{123}\); about 70 output words recover the state with complexity near \(2^{29.1}\). A long period is therefore not cryptographic security. The 64-bit/256-bit variants (KISS64/KISS11) have a larger state and period near \(2^{247}\), but remain statistical PRNGs; their parameters must not be mixed into the 32-bit formulas.
en.history: Marsaglia and Zaman proposed the KISS-style combination in 1993; the 1998 C version combined LCG, SHR3 and two MWC components into a four-word state; Rose’s 2018 analysis established the period bound and state-recovery attack. The 2009 64-bit KISS expanded the state to 256 bits and a period near \(2^{247}\). R128 also changes the catalog title from “lightweight block cipher” to “pseudorandom number generator”, because the old classification contradicts the algorithm.
